title.narrative: Strengthening Food Security and Livelihoods through Resilience and Sustainability in Yemen's Fisheries Sector

description.narrative: Overall objective: The resilience and income stability of coastal fishing families and their communities in Al-Mokha, Taiz, Yemen has been sustainably strengthened. Project Objective: 1,500 fishing families in Al-Mokha take advantage of the cooperative structures and the improved port infrastructure and improve their economic living conditions through lower catch losses and better marketing.

Target group and intervention area: 1,500 fishermen + 25 volunteers of the Fishing cooperative + 5 employees of ADO​ in Mohka (Taʿizz governorate).Total direct beneficiary group: 1,530 people (1500 fishermens + 25 Cooperative members + 5 Employees of ADO).Indirect beneficiaries: 10,500 people (1,500 fishing families), in line with the overall project objective.

Yemen's coastal fishing industry, which is crucial for food security, is severely impaired. Landing and distribution infrastructures are inadequate and the sector is experiencing a significant decline in catches. Crisis-related post-harvest losses exacerbate the situation.

participating-org.narrative: Germany - Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
